items.new: As the three boats lay there on that gently rolling sea, gazing down into its eternal blue noon — and as not a single groan or cry, not so much as a ripple or a bubble, came up from its depths — what landsman would have thought that beneath all that silence and peace, the greatest monster of the seas was writhing and wrenching in agony! Not eight inches of perpendicular rope were visible at the bows. Can it be believed that by three such thin threads the great Leviathan was suspended like the weight of an eight-day clock? Suspended? And from what? From three bits of board. Is this the creature of whom it was once so triumphantly said: "Can you fill his skin with barbed irons? Or his head with fish-spears? The sword of him that strikes at him cannot hold; the spear, the dart, nor the coat of mail. He regards iron as straw; the arrow cannot make him flee; darts are counted as stubble; he laughs at the shaking of a spear!" This the creature? This he? Oh, that prophecies should go unfulfilled! For with the strength of a thousand thighs in his tail, Leviathan had run his head under the mountains of the sea to hide from the Pequod's fish-spears!

items.new: But humane Starbuck was too late. The instant the dart struck, an ulcerous jet shot from that cruel wound. Goaded by it into more than bearable agony, the whale — now spouting thick blood — blindly charged the boats with savage fury, spattering them and their exulting crews all over with showers of gore, capsizing Flask's boat and damaging the bows. It was his death stroke. For by this time, so drained was he from blood loss that he helplessly rolled away from the wreck he had made, lay panting on his side, and impotently flapped his stumped fin. Then over and over he slowly revolved like a dying world, turned up the white secrets of his belly, lay like a log, and died. It was most pitiable, that last expiring spout. As when unseen hands gradually draw the water from some mighty fountain, and with half-stifled, melancholy gurglings the spray-column lowers and lowers to the ground — so fell the last long dying spout of the whale.

items.new: Now, this occasional inevitable sinking of the recently killed sperm whale is a very curious thing. No fisherman has yet adequately explained it. Usually the dead sperm whale floats with great buoyancy, its side or belly considerably elevated above the surface. If the only whales that sank this way were old, meager, broken-hearted creatures, with their pads of fat diminished and all their bones heavy and rheumatic, then you might reasonably argue that this sinking is caused by an uncommon density in the whale, resulting from this lack of buoyant matter in him. But it is not so. For young whales in the peak of health, swelling with noble aspirations, prematurely cut off in the warm flush and springtime of life with all their panting fat about them — even these strong, buoyant heroes sometimes sink.

items.new: It should be said, however, that the Sperm Whale is far less prone to this than any other species. Where one Sperm Whale goes down, twenty Right Whales do. This difference is no doubt largely due to the greater quantity of bone in the Right Whale. His Venetian blinds alone — the slatted baleen in his mouth — sometimes weigh more than a ton, and from this burden the Sperm Whale is wholly free. But there are instances where, after many hours or several days, the sunken whale rises again, more buoyant than in life. The reason is obvious. Gases are generated inside him. He swells to prodigious size and becomes a sort of animal balloon. A warship could hardly keep him under then. In the shore whaling, in the shallows among the bays of New Zealand, when a Right Whale shows signs of sinking, they fasten buoys to him with plenty of rope, so that when the body has gone down, they know where to look for it when it rises again.

Nevertheless, the fin-back's spout is so similar to the sperm whale's that unskilled fishermen often mistake it. And so Derick and all his men were now in valiant chase of this uncatchable brute. The Virgin, crowding on all sail, followed after her four young boats, and they all disappeared far to leeward, still in bold, hopeful pursuit.

items.new: The gallant Perseus, a son of Jupiter, was the first whaleman; and to the eternal honor of our calling, let it be said that the first whale our brotherhood ever attacked was not killed for any sordid motive. Those were the knightly days of our profession, when we took up arms only to rescue the distressed, and not to fill men's lamp-feeders. Everyone knows the fine story of Perseus and Andromeda: how the lovely Andromeda, a king's daughter, was tied to a rock on the seacoast, and just as Leviathan was in the very act of carrying her off, Perseus, the prince of whalemen, fearlessly advanced, harpooned the monster, and rescued and married the maiden. It was an admirable, artful feat, and one the best harpooners of today rarely achieve, since this Leviathan was killed with the very first throw. And let no one doubt this Arkite story; for in ancient Joppa, now Jaffa, on the Syrian coast, there stood for many ages, in one of the pagan temples, the vast skeleton of a whale, which the city's legends and all its inhabitants declared to be the very bones of the monster Perseus killed. When the Romans took Joppa, that same skeleton was carried to Italy in triumph. What seems most remarkable and suggestively important in this story is this: it was from Joppa that Jonah set sail.

items.new: If you reckon the largest sperm whale's tail to begin at the point of the trunk where it tapers to about the girth of a man, it covers an area on its upper surface alone of at least fifty square feet. The compact round root expands into two broad, firm, flat palms or flukes, gradually thinning to less than an inch in thickness. At the junction, these flukes slightly overlap, then recede sideways from each other like wings, leaving a wide gap between them. In no living thing are the lines of beauty more exquisitely defined than in the crescent borders of these flukes. At full expansion in a full-grown whale, the tail will considerably exceed twenty feet across.

items.new: Nor does this amazing strength at all cripple the graceful flexibility of its motions, where an infantlike ease undulates through a titanic power. On the contrary, those motions derive their most fearsome beauty from it. Real strength never impairs beauty or harmony but often bestows it. In everything impressively beautiful, strength has much to do with the magic. Take away the tied tendons that everywhere seem bursting from the marble in the carved Hercules, and its charm would be gone. When devout Eckerman lifted the linen sheet from Goethe's naked corpse, he was overwhelmed by the massive chest, which seemed like a Roman triumphal arch. When Angelo — Michelangelo — paints even God the Father in human form, mark what robustness is there. And whatever they may reveal of divine love in the Son, those soft, curled, hermaphroditic Italian paintings in which his image has been most successfully embodied — so destitute of all brawniness — hint nothing of any power but the merely negative, feminine one of submission and endurance, which by all accounts form the peculiar practical virtues of his teachings.

items.new: The casual comparison in this chapter between the whale and the elephant — so far as some aspects of the tail of the one and the trunk of the other are concerned — should not suggest those two opposite organs are equal, much less the creatures they belong to. For as the mightiest elephant is but a terrier to Leviathan, so compared with Leviathan's tail, his trunk is but the stalk of a lily. The most dreadful blow from the elephant's trunk would be as the playful tap of a fan compared with the measureless crush and crash of the sperm whale's ponderous flukes, which have repeatedly hurled entire boats with all their oars and crews into the air, much as an Indian juggler tosses his balls.*

items.new: The more I consider this mighty tail, the more I deplore my inability to express it. At times there are gestures in it that, though they would well grace the hand of man, remain wholly inexplicable. In an extensive herd, so remarkable, at times, are these mystic gestures that I have heard hunters declare them akin to Freemason signs and symbols — that the whale, by these methods, was intelligently conversing with the world. Nor are there lacking other motions of the whale in his general body, full of strangeness and unaccountable to his most experienced pursuer. Dissect him how I may, then, I only go skin deep. I do not know him, and never will. But if I cannot even understand the tail of this whale, how can I understand his head? Much more, how can I comprehend his face, when he has none? You shall see my back parts, my tail, he seems to say, but my face shall not be seen. But I cannot fully make out his back parts either. And hint what he will about his face — I say again he has no face.
